excluded_lineages: its unified-classifier configuration, provider-routing, run-origin and deterministic E2E descendants
PR 248, canonical merges, acceptance reports and host-memory summaries of the target

decisions.summary: Choose whether unified approval-model selection belongs to PA only or changes every product using the shared kernel.

accepted_outcomes: The final contract applies the configured unified selection to PA and leaves Coding CLI behavior unchanged unless that product independently opts into the generic kernel capability.
The kernel supports both an explicitly selected classifier model and omission that reuses the current run model, without embedding PA-specific policy.
rejected_outcomes: A mandatory global model switch that changes Coding CLI or every kernel consumer.
A channel-local implementation that covers only Web IM or only one PA Agent.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Historical semantic answer: the configured product scope is PA; the product-neutral kernel may expose explicit-model and reuse-current-model modes.

decisions.summary: Choose what happens when PA omits the unified approval-model setting.

accepted_outcomes: Omission preserves current behavior: each automatic classification reuses the triggering run or Agent model.
The default does not silently select a new global provider or model.
rejected_outcomes: Making the new field mandatory or changing the configured default merely by adding the option.
A hard-coded fallback model when the setting is absent.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Historical semantic answer: omission keeps the existing per-run model behavior.

decisions.summary: Choose whether an explicitly configured but unregistered approval model fails startup or silently degrades.

accepted_outcomes: PA rejects startup before serving work and identifies the invalid approval-model configuration.
The selected name is validated against the configured model catalog rather than a hard-coded provider list.
rejected_outcomes: Starting successfully while silently reusing each Agent model.
Deferring a known catalog mismatch until the first tool classification.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Historical semantic answer: an unregistered explicit selection is a startup configuration error, never a silent fallback.

decisions.summary: Choose whether the dedicated model affects only automatic permission classification or also replaces normal Agent reasoning.

accepted_outcomes: Only automatic allow, deny or ask classification uses the dedicated model.
The first normal Agent request and post-tool continuation remain on that run's own model.
rejected_outcomes: Changing the Agent's conversational, tool-continuation, compaction or unrelated hook model.
Applying the dedicated model to only one of the two classifier stages.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Historical semantic answer: the explicit model is classifier-only; normal and post-tool Agent turns retain their run model.

decisions.summary: Choose whether runtime failure of the explicitly selected classifier model may retry classification with another model.

accepted_outcomes: Retries allowed by the existing provider policy continue to target the same selected model.
After timeout, upstream error or unparseable output, classification enters the existing attended or unattended permission-failure path without trying the Agent model or another model.
rejected_outcomes: A C-to-Agent-model or C-to-default-model classification fallback.
Reporting that unified selection is enforced while silently changing model after an error.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Historical semantic answer: the selected model is a hard choice; runtime failure never changes classifier model.

decisions.summary: Choose whether configuration changes hot-update a running Gateway or take effect after restart.

accepted_outcomes: The Gateway reads and binds the choice at process startup; changing the file alone does not mutate the running kernel.
A restart validates and activates the new selection.
rejected_outcomes: A new hot-reload watcher or per-session update path added only for this field.
Claims that changing the file immediately affects an already-built kernel.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Historical semantic answer: the setting follows Gateway process configuration and changes only after restart.

decisions.summary: At the cutoff, both automatic classifier stages omit an explicit model, so HookContext resolves them through the current run model; the runtime already accepts an explicit hook model.

accepted_outcomes: The candidate traces both classifier calls through HookModelCall into runtime model and provider selection before designing the change.
It reuses the existing explicit hook-model capability or gives evidence for an equivalent smaller seam.
rejected_outcomes: A second LLM client or classifier runtime that duplicates existing provider routing.
Changing only a prompt or Agent default without controlling the classifier call model.

decisions.summary: PA owns its LLM catalog and process configuration, while agent.sdk is the only product-facing kernel construction seam.

accepted_outcomes: The design carries one optional selection from PA config through Gateway composition and the public SDK into the kernel-scoped classifier dependency.
The configured name is parsed, preserved on config save and validated against the catalog before useful runtime work begins.
rejected_outcomes: personal_assistant importing agent.core or agent.platform to set classifier internals.
Storing PA product policy in every Agent or session when one Gateway process owns the choice.

decisions.summary: All PA run origins share the same process kernel and canonical automatic classifier, including Agent-derived background work.

accepted_outcomes: The design covers user, heartbeat, cron and background_task origins without channel-specific copies of the selection.
Agent-derived work is identified by the actual cutoff origin and follows the same classifier dependency.
rejected_outcomes: Coverage limited to interactive Web IM requests.
Using a nonexistent subagent origin or requiring each origin to carry duplicate model metadata.

decisions.summary: Model routing must be verified from actual provider request identities and complete request sequences, not from generated prose.

accepted_outcomes: Explicit mode proves A to C to A and B to C to B across normal, classifier and post-tool requests; omission proves A to A to A and B to B to B.
Cross-provider tests use distinct clients or equivalent observable provider boundaries, and failure records no Agent-model reclassification.
Equivalent deterministic fixtures and sequence notation receive full credit.
rejected_outcomes: Asserting model routing from response wording or a private setter alone.
A single override client that cannot prove the selected model reached the correct provider.
oracle.acceptance_notes: The historical symbols A, B and C are oracle notation, not required public names or implementation identifiers.

decisions.summary: The solution must preserve package direction and keep the kernel product-neutral while exposing a bounded consumer option.

accepted_outcomes: PA depends only on agent.sdk, core remains independent of platform, and IM remains independent of agent.
The public kernel construction contract remains generic and omission-compatible; Coding CLI need not add configuration.
rejected_outcomes: A PA branch inside core, a PA import of kernel internals or a restored kernel HTTP control surface.
Adding per-product model names to a generic connection/catalog DTO without a demonstrated need.

decisions.summary: The kernel-scoped selection needs one canonical injection path into the built-in auto gate, but equivalent narrow mechanisms are acceptable.

accepted_outcomes: A registry-scoped dependency, trusted built-in dependency bundle or equivalent one-per-kernel seam can pass when only the canonical classifier consumes it and no session or Agent copy becomes authoritative.
The design explains ownership, validation, lifecycle and deletion or migration of any temporary bridge.
rejected_outcomes: Two simultaneous injection protocols, a module-global mutable selection or per-call lookup from the config file.
Requiring historical helper names or state keys without an architectural reason.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Judge the single-owner semantics, not the historical extension-state helper or its exact key.
